slides.title: Understanding Data Distribution
bullets: Data can be organized into categories for comparison
Bar charts display frequency or magnitude across groups
Each bar represents a distinct category of measurement
Height of bar indicates the value for that category
narration: Data can be organized into categories for comparison
This slide shows how categories fit together

slides.title: Measures of Central Tendency
bullets: Mean represents the arithmetic average of a dataset
Median is the middle value when data is ordered
Mode is the most frequently occurring value
These measures summarize the center of a distribution
narration: Median is the middle value when data is ordered
This measure finds the center point

slides.title: Trends Over Time
bullets: Line charts show how variables change across time periods
Upward slope indicates increase in the measured variable
Downward slope indicates decrease over the timeframe
Data points are connected to reveal patterns
narration: Data points are connected to reveal patterns
Lines connect items to show trends

slides.title: Variability and Spread
bullets: Range is the difference between highest and lowest values
Standard deviation measures average distance from mean
Variance is the square of the standard deviation
Spread indicates how clustered or dispersed data is
narration: Spread indicates how clustered or dispersed data is
This shows how spread out values are
